correctness.rationale: For nonempty feasible patterns the maximum symbol multiplicity h gives LCS>=h and |u|<=min(k,sum_i min(c_i,h)); a reverse-block u has LCS exactly h and can saturate the capacity bound. For the quotient plateau, LCS>=ceil(|u|/q) and pure-letter probes distinguish capped counts; balanced opposite blocks attain the threshold and force a strict split below it. The empty host and one-symbol alphabet are explicitly handled. Independent bounded exhaustive dynamic-programming tests passed 191852 plateau instances plus 34188 content-envelope host/pattern comparisons; the general proof is combinatorial and is not inferred from tests.

This gives the exact minimal quotient index transition for all finite alphabets and all k, with explicit separating constructions, plus a sharp content-dependent minimax disorder invariant.
